test_title: PYST 13: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 13 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following schemes on Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) encourages entrepreneurs to set up CBG plants, produce and supply CBG to Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) for sale as automotive and industrial fuels?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation (SATAT)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation (SATAT)** scheme was launched by the Government of India in **October 2018**. It aims to promote the use of **Compressed Bio Gas (CBG)** as an alternative, renewable fuel.
 
• The scheme encourages **entrepreneurs** to set up CBG plants and produce fuel using agricultural residue, municipal solid waste, and other biodegradable waste. *Hence, the statement in the question is correct.*
 
• Under SATAT, **Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs)**, such as Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL), are authorized to procure CBG produced by these plants.
 
• The scheme aims to achieve environmental sustainability by reducing dependence on fossil fuels and promoting cleaner fuel alternatives. It also aligns with India's commitment to reducing **carbon emissions** under the Paris Agreement.
 
• SATAT provides significant opportunities for rural entrepreneurship and employment, as setting up CBG plants involves local resources and manpower. *Hence, this is a key initiative for sustainable transportation.*
 
• CBG under SATAT can be used as an **automotive fuel**, industrial fuel, and for power generation. It can also serve as a replacement for conventional natural gas.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation (SATAT).***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation (SATAT):**

 
 
• Launched by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas in **2018**, SATAT is a significant initiative to promote **bio-energy** and reduce India's reliance on fossil fuels.
 
• The scheme supports the establishment of **CBG plants** and their integration into the fuel ecosystem, thereby promoting waste management and energy efficiency.
 
• SATAT also contributes to achieving India's **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)** under the **Paris Agreement** by reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
 
 
 
• **Compressed Bio Gas (CBG):**
 
 
• **CBG** is produced through the anaerobic decomposition of organic waste such as agricultural residue, cattle dung, and municipal solid waste.
 
• It is a renewable, cleaner fuel that can replace **natural gas**, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), and coal in industrial applications.
 
• CBG is also used for automotive purposes, offering a greener alternative to conventional fuels like diesel and petrol.
 
 
 
• **Role of Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs):**
 
 
• OMCs such as IOCL, BPCL, and HPCL play a pivotal role in the SATAT initiative by procuring CBG from producers.
 
• They ensure the distribution and accessibility of CBG across the country, integrating it into the energy supply chain.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of SATAT:**

 
 
• The SATAT initiative aims to set up **5000 CBG plants** across India by **2023-24**, producing approximately **15 million tonnes** of CBG annually.
 
• It promotes the use of **compressed biogas** as a sustainable and affordable alternative to conventional fuels.
 
• The initiative supports **waste-to-energy** programs and contributes to effective waste management practices in rural and urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Schemes:**
 
 
• **Biogas Programme:** This scheme focuses on the production of biogas for cooking and lighting purposes, primarily aimed at rural areas.
 
• **Waste to Energy Programme:** This initiative promotes technologies to convert municipal waste into energy but does not specifically address CBG production for OMCs.
 
• **Cent Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) Scheme:** While it promotes CBG production, it is not as comprehensive as SATAT in supporting entrepreneurs and integrating CBG into the fuel market.
